CITY OF

  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  4045 PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH • ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274
  TELEPHONE 310.377.1577 • FAX 310.377.4468
  www.RollingHillsEstates.gov

  Adjourned Meeting Agenda
  CITY COUNCIL

Tuesday, December 16, 2025  7:00 PM  Council Chamber

NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's web site under City Council Meeting agendas at www.RollingHillsEstates.gov and
  during regular business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's web
  site and a recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP -TV
  Channel 35 (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome on any item during City Council consideration of the item. An opportunity is
  also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If you would like to
  address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public comment, please
  complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

3.  ROLL CALL

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

  NONE

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the
  City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member
  prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on separately.)

  A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS
  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the
  City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by
  title only.

 City Council  Adjourned Meeting Agenda  December 16, 2025

  B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF NOVEMBER & DECEMBER 2025
  Recommendation: Approve warrants 69094 through 69162 in the amount of
  $774,573.84 and Supplemental Warrants 110425 through 110525; 120125 through
  120325; in the amount of $235,424.37; for a grand total amount of $1,009,998.21

  F.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF DECEMBER 8, 2025
  Recommendation: Receive and file
  Attachments: Draft Minutes

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS
  This is the appropriate time for members of the public to make comments regarding items not listed on this
  agenda. If you would like to address the City Council, please complete a speaker sheet and give to the
  City Clerk. Under the State's open meeting law - the Brown Act - no action may be taken on any item not
  on the agenda.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  NONE

City Clerk's office at (310) 377-1577 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.
 City Council  Adjourned Meeting Agenda  December 16, 2025

8.  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

  Memorandum from Lauren Pettit, City Clerk
  Recommendation: That the City Council consider postponing the selection of the
  Mayor until the January 27, 2026 City Council meeting and nominate and appoint a
  Mayor Pro Tem on December 16 to ensure continued Council leadership support
  and representation during the interim period, with the current Mayor remaining in the
  role until that time.
  Attachments: Staff Report

  B.  PROPOSAL FOR HISTORIC PRESERVATION CONSULTING SERVICES

  Memorandum from Jeannie Naughton, Community Development & Public Works
  Director
  Recommendation: That the City Council approve: 1) A Master Professional Services
  Agreement (MPSA) with Architectural Resources Group (ARG) for historic
  preservation consulting services, subject to approval as to form by the City Attorney;
  and 2) TaskOrder No. 2025-01, authorizing services to update Rolling Hills Estates
  Municipal Code (RHEMC) Chapter 17.38 - Landmark Overlay Zones, subject to
  approval as to form by the City Attorney.
  Attachments: Staff Report

  C.  MASTER PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT AND TASK ORDER
  WITH MENDOZA ENGINEERING FOR STREET AND SIDEWALK REPAIR
  SERVICES
  Memorandum from Kirsten Graham, Public Works Manager
  Recommendation: That the City Council approve: 1) A Master Professional Services
  Agreement (MPSA) with Mendoza Engineering for on-call asphalt street and
  sidewalk repair work, subject to approval as to form by the City Attorney; and 2)
  Task Order 2025-01, under the MPSA, in the not-to-exceed amount of $33,462
  ($30,420 plus a 10% contingency) for asphalt and sidewalk repairs at various
  locations throughout the City, as outlined in this report, subject to approval as to form
  by the City Attorney.
  Attachments: Staff Report

CITY COUNCIL  Page 3
12/16/2025
Americans With Disabilities Act: In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you require a disability-related
modification or accommodation to attend or participate in this meeting, including auxiliary aids or services, please call the
City Clerk's office at (310) 377-1577 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.
 City Council  Adjourned Meeting Agenda  December 16, 2025

  D.  INTRODUCTION  OF  ORDINANCE  NO. 759 AMENDING RHEMC
  CHAPTER 3.38 (UPCCAA ADOPTION) AND ORDINANCE NO. 760
  ADDING RHEMC CHAPTER 3.40 (PUBLIC PROJECT CONTRACTING
  POLICY)
  Memorandum from Donald M. Davis, City Attorney
  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Introduce for a first reading proposed
  Ordinance No. 759 amending and restating municipal code chapter 3.38 (re-titled
  “Public Project Contracting - UPCCAA Adoption”) and bring back the ordinance
  for a second reading and adoption at the City Council meeting on January 13, 2026;
  and 2) Introduce for a first reading proposed Ordinance No. 760 adding municipal
  code chapter 3.40 (“Public Project Contracting Policy”) and bring back the
  ordinance for a second reading and adoption at the City Council meeting on January
  13, 2026.
  Attachments: Staff Report

  E.  REVIEW OF PROPOSED PUBLIC PROJECT CONTRACTING POLICY

  Memorandum from Donald M. Davis, City Attorney
  Recommendation: That the City Council review and provide comments on the
  proposed Public Project Contracting Policy, and direct staff to bring back the Policy
  for adoption by resolution at the City Council meeting on January 13, 2026.
  Attachments: Staff Report

  F.  TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEMS: 1) SPEED LIMIT SIGN
  RECOMMENDATIONS AND 2) RIGHT-TURN ON RED AT THE
  NORTHWEST CORNER OF PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE EAST
  Memorandum from Kirsten Graham, Public Works Manager
  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Approve the Traffic and Safety
  Committee’s recommendation to install three speed limit signs along Palos Verdes
  Drive North (PVDN) as reviewed and recommended by the City’s Traffic
  Engineering Deputy; and 2) Approve the Committee’s recommendation to install an
  additional edge lit speed limit sign in front of City Hall to enhance visibility of the
  newly adopted speed limit; and 3) Approve the installation of a “No Right Turn on
  Red” sign at the northwest corner of Palos Verdes Drive North and Palos Verdes
  Drive East based on the safety analysis provided by the City’s traffic engineering
  consultant; and 4) Authorize staff to proceed with procurement and installation of the
  signs.
  Attachments: Staff Report

CITY COUNCIL  Page 4
12/16/2025
Americans With Disabilities Act: In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you require a disability-related
modification or accommodation to attend or participate in this meeting, including auxiliary aids or services, please call the
City Clerk's office at (310) 377-1577 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.
 City Council  Adjourned Meeting Agenda  December 16, 2025

  G.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 2613 ESTABLISHING  THE  DROP-IN
  OPEN PLAY PICKLEBALL PROGRAMMING FEE
  Memorandum from Alexa Davis, Assistant City Manager and Rosa Pinuelas,
  Community Services Supervisor
  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2613 updating Section
  5 of the City’s Fees and Charges Schedule for Fiscal Year 2025-26 to include a
  drop-in open play pickleball fee of $5 per person per day/visit.
  Attachments: Staff Report

9.  OLD BUSINESS

  A.  FISCAL YEAR 2025-2026 WORKPLAN UPDATE

  Memorandum from Greg Grammer, City Manager
  Recommendation: Receive and file.
  Attachments: Staff Report

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

11.  CITY COUNCIL / REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS
  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to
  other Members of the City Council and the public on any issues or activities of Council Committees, ad
  hoc committees, regional or state-wide governmental associations, special districts, joint powers
  authorities and the various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or have an
  interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS
  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to request information on currently
  pending projects and/or issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration
  and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

13.  CLOSED SESSION
  If you would like to address the City Council regarding an item on the Closed Session agenda, please
  contact the City Manager or City Clerk. Any reportable action taken in Closed Session will be reported
  in Open Session.

  NONE

14.  ADJOURNMENT
  Next meeting: Tuesday, January 13, 2025

CITY COUNCIL  Page 5
12/16/2025

  $774,573.84 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 110425 THROUGH

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

  Recommendation: That the City Council consider postponing the selection of the
  Mayor until the January 27, 2026 City Council meeting and nominate and appoint a
  Mayor Pro Tem on December 16 to ensure continued Council leadership support and
  representation during the interim period, with the current Mayor remaining in the role
  until that time.

City Clerk Pettit provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  POSTPONE THE SELECTION OF MAYOR UNTIL JANUARY 27, 2026, WITH
  THE CURRENT MAYOR REMAINING IN THE ROLE UNTIL THAT TIME.

MAYOR STEGURA nominated COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER to serve as the City’s next
MAYOR PRO TEM.

  PAM BROWN SCHACHTER  APPOINTED  MAYOR  PRO  TEM  BY
  ACCLAMATION.

B.  PROPOSAL FOR HISTORIC PRESERVATION CONSULTING SERVICES

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve: 1) A Master Professional Services
  Agreement (MPSA) with Architectural Resources Group (ARG) for historic
  preservation consulting services, subject to approval as to form by the City Attorney;
  and 2) Task Order No. 2025-01, authorizing services to update Rolling Hills Estates
  Municipal Code (RHEMC) Chapter 17.38 - Landmark Overlay Zones, subject to
  approval as to form by the City Attorney.

Community Development & Public Works Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per
the agenda material).

Council Members expressed strong support, citing the importance of preserving historic
resources and community character, and concerns that protections could be overridden without
updated code standards.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
DECEMBER 16, 2025
   COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE: 1) A MASTER PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
  (MPSA) WITH ARCHITECTURAL RESOURCES GROUP (ARG) FOR
  HISTORIC PRESERVATION CONSULTING SERVICES, SUBJECT TO
  APPROVAL AS TO FORM BY THE CITY ATTORNEY; AND 2) TASK ORDER
  NO. 2025-01, AUTHORIZING SERVICES TO UPDATE ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE (RHEMC) CHAPTER 17.38 - LANDMARK
  OVERLAY ZONES, SUBJECT TO APPROVAL AS TO FORM BY THE CITY
  ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

C.  MASTER PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT AND TASK ORDER WITH
  MENDOZA ENGINEERING FOR STREET AND SIDEWALK REPAIR SERVICES

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve: 1) A Master Professional Services
  Agreement (MPSA) with Mendoza Engineering for on-call asphalt street and sidewalk
  repair work, subject to approval as to form by the City Attorney; and 2) Task Order
  2025-01, under the MPSA, in the not-to-exceed amount of $33,462 ($30,420 plus a
  10% contingency) for asphalt and sidewalk repairs at various locations throughout
  the City, as outlined in this report, subject to approval as to form by the City Attorney.

Public Works Manager Graham provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Council discussed when the City uses on-call services versus bidding each project and
confirmed that task order numbering resets with each master agreement.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE: 1) A MASTER PUBLIC WORKS AGREEMENT (MPWA) WITH
  MENDOZA ENGINEERING FOR ON-CALL ASPHALT STREET AND
  SIDEWALK REPAIR WORK, SUBJECT TO APPROVAL AS TO FORM BY THE
  CITY ATTORNEY; AND 2) TASK ORDER 2025-01, UNDER THE MPWA, IN
  THE NOT-TO-EXCEED AMOUNT OF $33,462 ($30,420 PLUS A 10%
  CONTINGENCY) FOR ASPHALT AND SIDEWALK REPAIRS AT VARIOUS
  LOCATIONS THROUGHOUT THE CITY, AS OUTLINED IN THIS REPORT,
  SUBJECT TO APPROVAL AS TO FORM BY THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

D.  INTRODUCTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 759 AMENDING RHEMC CHAPTER 3.38
  (UPCCAA ADOPTION) AND ORDINANCE NO. 760 ADDING RHEMC CHAPTER 3.40
  (PUBLIC PROJECT CONTRACTING POLICY)

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Introduce for a first reading proposed
  Ordinance No. 759 amending and restating municipal code chapter 3.38 (re-titled
  “Public Project Contracting - UPCCAA Adoption”) and bring back the ordinance for a
  second reading and adoption at the City Council meeting on January 13, 2026; and
  2) Introduce for a first reading proposed Ordinance No. 760 adding municipal code
  chapter 3.40 (“Public Project Contracting Policy”) and bring back the ordinance for a
  second reading and adoption at the City Council meeting on January 13, 2026.

City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
DECEMBER 16, 2025
 Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  INTRODUCE FOR FIRST READING PROPOSED ORDINANCE NO. 759
  AMENDING AND RESTATING MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 3.38 (RE-
  TITLED “PUBLIC PROJECT CONTRACTING - UPCCAA ADOPTION”) AND
  DIRECT STAFF TO BRING BACK THE ORDINANCE FOR SECOND
  READING AND ADOPTION AT THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING ON JANUARY
  13, 2026.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance No. 759 by title.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  INTRODUCE FOR FIRST READING PROPOSED ORDINANCE NO. 760
  ADDING MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 3.40 (“PUBLIC PROJECT
  CONTRACTING POLICY”) AND DIRECT STAFF TO BRING BACK THE
  ORDINANCE FOR SECOND READING AND ADOPTION AT THE CITY
  COUNCIL MEETING ON JANUARY 13, 2026.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance No. 760 by title.

E.  REVIEW OF PROPOSED PUBLIC PROJECT CONTRACTING POLICY

  Recommendation: That the City Council review and provide comments on the
  proposed Public Project Contracting Policy, and direct staff to bring back the Policy
  for adoption by resolution at the City Council meeting on January 13, 2026.

City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Council discussed consistency of “may” vs. “will” language regarding awarding contracts,
authority limits, budget safeguards, ethics/conflict-of-interest compliance (including staff Form
700 filing), and the operational benefit of clear procedures and on-call contracting for routine
repairs.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  DIRECT STAFF TO RETURN THE PROPOSED PUBLIC PROJECT
  CONTRACTING POLICY FOR ADOPTION BY RESOLUTION AT THE
  JANUARY 13, 2026 CITY COUNCIL MEETING.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

F.  TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEMS: 1) SPEED LIMIT SIGN
  RECOMMENDATIONS AND 2) RIGHT-TURN ON RED AT THE NORTHWEST
  CORNER OF PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
DECEMBER 16, 2025
   Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Approve the Traffic and Safety
  Committee’s recommendation to install three speed limit signs along Palos Verdes
  Drive North (PVDN) as reviewed and recommended by the City’s Traffic Engineering
  Deputy; and 2) Approve the Committee’s recommendation to install an additional
  edge lit speed limit sign in front of City Hall to enhance visibility of the newly adopted
  speed limit; and 3) Approve the installation of a “No Right Turn on Red” sign at the
  northwest corner of Palos Verdes Drive North and Palos Verdes Drive East based on
  the safety analysis provided by the City’s traffic engineering consultant; and 4)
  Authorize staff to proceed with procurement and installation of the signs.

Public Works Director Graham provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Staff confirmed the edge-lit sign would be replacing as current speed limit sign, and not be an
additional sign in the location, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE COMMITTEE’S RECOMMENDATION TO INSTALL AN
  ADDITIONAL EDGE LIT SPEED LIMIT SIGN IN FRONT OF CITY HALL TO
  ENHANCE VISIBILITY OF THE NEWLY ADOPTED SPEED LIMIT.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
Public testimony was received from resident and Traffic and Safety Committee member David
Rowe, who spoke in support of the additional speed limit signs.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE  THE  TRAFFIC  AND  SAFETY  COMMITTEE’S
  RECOMMENDATION TO INSTALL THREE SPEED LIMIT SIGNS ALONG
  PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH (PVDN) AS REVIEWED AND
  RECOMMENDED BY THE CITY’S TRAFFIC ENGINEERING DEPUTY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

Public Works Director Graham provided further information on the “no right turn on red” sign
at the northwest corner of Palos Verdes Drive North and Palos Verdes Drive East and
introduced the City’s Traffic Engineer Wes Pringle.

The Traffic Engineer cited skewed intersection geometry, sightline obstructions (including a
median signal pole and tree), and increased pedestrian activity (including park/playground
area). He noted that acciddent history did not show recorded collisions at the intersection, but
staff recommended the restriction as a precautionary safety measure. Staff noted that if
queuing issues arise, signal timing could be evaluated.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
Public testimony was received from resident Lynn Yen, who spoke in support of the “no right
turn on red” sign.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHACHTER,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE INSTALLATION OF A “NO RIGHT TURN ON RED” SIGN AT
  THE NORTHWEST CORNER OF PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND
  PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST BASED ON THE SAFETY ANALYSIS
  PROVIDED BY THE CITY’S TRAFFIC ENGINEERING CONSULTANT; AND
  AUTHORIZE STAFF TO PROCEED WITH PROCUREMENT AND
  INSTALLATION OF THE SIGNS.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
DECEMBER 16, 2025
   AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

G.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 2613 ESTABLISHING THE DROP-IN OPEN PLAY
  PICKLEBALL PROGRAMMING FEE

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2613 updating Section
  5 of the City’s Fees and Charges Schedule for Fiscal Year 2025-26 to include a drop-
  in open play pickleball fee of $5 per person per day/visit.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

Staff explained that the Park and Activities Commission reviewed the pilot program and
recommended the fee and scheduling adjustments; Council previously approved program
recommendations, and this resolution formally updates the adopted fee schedule.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2613 UPDATING SECTION 5 OF THE CITY’S
  FEES AND CHARGES SCHEDULE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2025-26 TO INCLUDE
  A DROP-IN OPEN PLAY PICKLEBALL FEE OF $5 PER PERSON PER
  DAY/VISIT.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2613 by title.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  FISCAL YEAR 2025-2026 WORKPLAN UPDATE

  Recommendation: Receive and file.

City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), highlighting the
progress toward George F Canyon Nature Center project with construction coordination and
inspection services anticipated to return to the Council in January and groundbreaking
anticipated in early 2026. He also highlighted the Palos Verdes Drive North / Palos Verdes
Drive East intersection improvement project funding update (including Measure M
components), with construction timing coordinated around school session. He provided
updates on the Local Hazard Mitigation Plan process and anticipated committee and
commission review schedule of early 2026, as well as updates on the parks & recreation study
and code/process improvements (including alarm permit/false alarm changes). Lastly, he
provided a status update regarding the Peter Weber Equestrian Center
monitoring/coordination and ongoing work program items.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

There being no objection, MAYOR STEGURA so ordered.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
DECEMBER 16, 2025
 10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

City Attorney Davis reported that the City Attorney’s office has created a compilation of the text
of Brown Act in effect as of January 1, 2026, which will be provided to the City Council,
